memory_update.text: GEV is the highest-confidence direct equipment candidate for the gas turbine and grid-equipment bottleneck; next pass should check backlog quality, production expansion, and OEM competitive landscape versus Siemens Energy and Mitsubishi Heavy, which are not primary US-listed common stocks.

BKR should remain in the universe as an LNG and gas-infrastructure equipment supplier; inclusion depends on evidence that compression/turbomachinery procurement is capacity constrained and material to backlog.
WMB is a strong midstream candidate because it has a disclosed data-center pipeline-capacity agreement; track whether additional gas-to-data-center contracts enter backlog.

The node appears to be a deliverability stack rather than a single commodity trade: turbine slots, LNG export ramp, pipeline capacity, gas basis, utility regulatory approvals, and transmission all interact.

Potential omitted candidates for later expansion include Energy Transfer, Kinder Morgan, TC Energy, Fluor, KBR, Chart Industries, Venture Global, Vistra, NRG, and Bloom Energy; they were excluded here only due to the five-candidate limit.

node: Dispatchable gas generation, gas turbines, pipelines, and LNG
summary: Expanded universe for the dispatchable gas power / LNG chokepoint. The strongest public-market mappings are gas-turbine OEM capacity, LNG compression and power-generation equipment, gas pipeline deliverability into data-center and power-load clusters, LNG export capacity ramp timing, and regulated utilities with large gas-generation buildouts. This is research support only, not a trading recommendation.
